newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India up with Bombay, Taiwan slips.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India up with Bombay, Taiwan slips.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts extended mild gains on Tuesday following a pick up in local stocks, but traders said the market remained slow with no clear trend.
"There was really nothing in the market until the last few minutes in Bombay, when things frothed up a bit," said a GDR trader. He said interest in London was centred on Reliance, Hindalco and ICICI.
Hindalco picked up 31 cents to $34.50/35.40 and ICICI added 25 cents to $15.75/16.75 following results on Monday.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.29 points firmer at 84.57, a 0.35 percent rise, with the premium over the local market at 19.46 percent from 19.93 percent.
The Cazenove Indian GDR index added 0.46 points to 95.42 -- a 19.24 percent premium to the local market. It measures from midday on the previous trading day to midday today.
Bombay's benchmark index rose 36.10 points to 4,217.58.

Taiwanese GDRs came under pressure following a bout of profit-taking in technology shares in Taipei. Traders said the local market's push through 10,000 points in intra-day trade was encouraging, but tech-heavy GDRs lost ground.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index shed 2.14 points, or 1.45 percent, to 140.82, representing a discount to the local market of 1.45 percent.
Taiwan's weighted index lost 30.71 points on the day to 9,892.34.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index shed 1.79 points to 75.13 points, a premium of 45.43 percent over the local market.
